mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, increasing equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 3.5% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A UNRATE above 4.5% signals a weak labor market, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as weak labor conditions often precede economic slowdowns and equity sell-offs.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 4.5% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising CPIAUCSL (inflation) combined with FEDFUNDS below 3.5% signals an overheating economy that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 3 months AND FEDFUNDS < 3.5%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 3 months and FEDFUNDS < 3.5% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime (INDPRO < 100), declining industrial production signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO < 100 (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as strong housing activity signals robust economic growth and rising consumer confidence, boosting equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above 1200 (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL above 2.5% signals persistent inflation, which may lead to aggressive monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising HOUST (housing starts) combined with a rising RSAFS (residential fixed investment) signals robust economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 0.5% in 3 months AND RSAFS rises > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises > 0.5% in 3 months and RSAFS rises > 0.5% in 3 months (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a strong labor market regime (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in 3 months), S&P 500 forward returns are positive over the next 60 trading days, as robust employment growth supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in 3 months (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
